learningObjectives: Install Tricentis Tosca On-Premises on a Windows machine.
Request and activate a valid Tosca training license via the Tricentis Support Hub.
Install the Tricentis Automation Extension in Google Chrome.
Verify that all three prerequisites are working correctly before starting the course.
Understand the macOS workaround (Windows VM) required to run Tosca.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Overview: What You Need Before Starting

elements.description: To begin the AS1 course, ensure you have all three of the following:
items: Tricentis Tosca On-Premises installed on your machine
A valid Tosca license (request via the Tricentis Support Hub)
Tricentis Automation Extension installed in Google Chrome

elements.description: The course SUT is the Tricentis Demo Web Shop — hosted online, no local server setup required.

elements.title: Open the SUT in your browser to verify access:

items.label: Tricentis Demo Web Shop
items.note: must be reachable from inside your Windows VM

bulletPoints: SUT URL: https://demowebshop.tricentis.com — open it in Chrome to verify access.
Tosca version used in the course: 14.x (minor UI differences possible in other versions).

elements.title: Windows Installation
items: Download the Tosca On-Premises installer from the Tricentis website (login required).
Right-click the installer → Run as Administrator.
Follow the setup wizard — accept the default installation path.
Tosca Commander launches automatically after installation completes.
Confirm Tosca Commander opens without errors before proceeding.

elements.title: macOS Installation (via Windows VM)
items: Install a Windows VM on your Mac — choose one of the three options below.
Install Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit) inside the VM.
Allocate at least 4 GB RAM and 2 CPU cores to the VM for acceptable performance.
Follow the Windows installation steps above inside the VM.

elements.title: Minimum System Requirements (Windows guest)
items: OS: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit)
RAM: 8 GB minimum, 16 GB recommended
Disk: 10 GB free space
.NET Framework 4.7.2 or higher (pre-installed on Win 10/11)
Google Chrome browser

bulletPoints: VM users: allocate RAM generously — Tosca + Windows together need at least 8 GB total.
Do not use 32-bit Windows — Tosca requires a 64-bit OS.

elements.description: Free training licenses are requested at support-hub.tricentis.com. You need a Tricentis account (free registration) to submit a ticket.

elements.title: License Activation (after receiving the .lic file)
items: Open Tosca Commander.
Navigate to: Help → License → Import License File.
Browse to the .lic file received from Tricentis.
Click Open — Tosca confirms activation with a success message.

elements.text: Training licenses are typically valid for 30–90 days. Request yours 1–2 days before you plan to start the course — activation is not instant.

bulletPoints: If activation fails: ensure the .lic file matches the machine's hardware ID (displayed in the License dialog).
License expired mid-course? Submit a renewal request via the same Support Hub process.

elements.term: Tosca keeps showing a license pop-up on launch?
elements.description: This usually means Tosca Commander isn't connected to a valid license source. If your organization uses a Cloud License Server (instead of, or in addition to, a local .lic file), connect Tosca directly to it.

elements.title: Connect to your Cloud License Server
items: Double-check with your administrator that you've been added to the Cloud License Server — you can only connect to servers you have a user account on.
In Tosca Commander, access the license configuration, go to the Setup tab, and select Change connection.
On the next screen, select Connect to Cloud hosted License Server, then click OK.
On the next screen, sign in with your Tricentis Support Hub credentials. If your organization uses a proxy server, activate the Use default proxy checkbox on the sign-in screen.
A successful connection takes you directly to the Tosca start screen — the license pop-up should not reappear.

items.label: Connect to your cloud license server

bulletPoints: Cloud License Server connection is separate from importing a local .lic file (Step 2 above) — use whichever method your organization/training license actually relies on.
Still stuck? Check with your Tosca administrator whether your account has been granted access to the specific Cloud License Server your organization uses.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Step 3: Install the Tricentis Automation Extension

elements.description: The Tricentis Automation Extension is a Chrome browser plugin that enables XScan to inspect and interact with web application elements. Without it, web automation is not possible.

elements.title: Installation (Windows / Inside VM)
items: Open Google Chrome (inside the Windows VM for macOS users).
Go to the Chrome Web Store — search 'Tricentis Automation Extension'.
Click Add to Chrome → Add Extension.
Confirm the Tricentis icon appears in the Chrome extensions toolbar (top-right).
Right-click the icon → Pin to toolbar for easy access.

items.label: Tricentis Automation Extension — Chrome Web Store

elements.text: macOS VM users: the extension must be installed in Chrome INSIDE the Windows VM — not in the Chrome browser on your macOS host. Tosca can only communicate with the local VM Chrome instance.

bulletPoints: The extension must be ENABLED (not just installed) before running XScan.
XScan fails if Chrome is running as Administrator — both Tosca and Chrome must run at the same privilege level.

elements.title: Pre-course Checklist — all 3 must be green
items: Tosca Commander opens without errors and shows license as active
Tricentis Automation Extension icon is visible and enabled in Chrome (inside VM for macOS users)
https://demowebshop.tricentis.com loads correctly in Chrome

elements.title: Common Issues & Fixes
items: Tosca: 'No valid license found' → re-import the .lic via Help → License → Import License File
XScan cannot detect browser → check Chrome is not running as Administrator
VM is very slow → increase RAM allocation to at least 4 GB in VM settings
macOS: XScan finds nothing → ensure extension is installed in the VM Chrome, not the host Chrome

bulletPoints: Do not start Lesson 01 until all three checklist items are confirmed.
If the license check fails: verify your machine's hardware ID matches the .lic file.

elements.text: Finishing AS1 does not end with a formal certification exam like Pega's CSA/CPBA. It ends with the course's final quiz, which earns you a Badge and points — not a Certificate. Badges appear on your Academy "Badges" page with a shareable verification link; Certificates appear on the "Courses" page as a downloadable PDF.

elements.term: Certificate vs Badges: What is the difference?
elements.description: The Tricentis Academy offers a robust certification program recognising users' skillsets, capabilities, and project readiness. This program provides curated learning journeys intended to enable partners to build competence within specific testing roles. Each path is designed with self-paced online learning, consisting of carefully chosen courses covering skills necessary for success in each role.

examPitfalls.title: Tosca does NOT run on macOS natively
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume Tosca works on macOS like most modern tools. It does not — it is Windows-only.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: macOS users must use a Windows VM. The extension must also be installed in Chrome INSIDE the VM.

examPitfalls.title: Extension must be in the VM browser, not the host browser
examPitfalls.trapDescription: macOS VM users install the extension in the macOS Chrome but cannot understand why XScan fails.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Tricentis Automation Extension must be installed in the Chrome browser running inside the Windows VM — not on the macOS host.

examPitfalls.title: License request takes time — plan ahead
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates install Tosca and expect to start immediately, not realising the license must be requested and may take 1–2 business days to arrive.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Request your Tricentis training license before you plan to start. Do not wait until you are ready to begin Lesson 01.

examPitfalls.title: XScan fails when Chrome runs as Administrator
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running Chrome with elevated privileges (Run as Administrator) causes XScan to fail to detect the browser.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Run Chrome at normal (non-elevated) privilege. Tosca and Chrome must run at the same privilege level for XScan to work.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester uses a MacBook Pro and wants to complete the Tricentis Tosca AS1 course. What is the correct setup approach?

options.text: Install Tricentis Tosca for macOS from the Tricentis website.
Tosca is not compatible with macOS hardware at all — a physical Windows PC is required.
Run Tosca via a web browser on macOS — no installation is needed.
Use Boot Camp or a Windows VM (e.g., Parallels, VMware Fusion, VirtualBox) to run Windows, then install Tosca inside the Windows environment.

practiceQuiz.hint: Tosca is Windows-only — macOS needs a Windows runtime environment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tricentis Tosca On-Premises is a Windows-only application. macOS users must install a Windows virtual machine (Parallels Desktop, VMware Fusion, or VirtualBox) and install Tosca inside the Windows guest OS. There is no native macOS version.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Windows user has installed Tosca and received their license file (.lic). What is the next step to activate the license?

options.text: In Tosca Commander: Help → License → Import License File → browse to the .lic file.
Double-click the .lic file — it auto-registers with Tosca.
Email the .lic file to Tricentis support and wait for remote activation.
Place the .lic file in the Tosca installation folder — it is detected automatically on next launch.

practiceQuiz.hint: Manual import via the Help menu.
practiceQuiz.rationale: License activation requires manually importing the .lic file: Tosca Commander → Help → License → Import License File. Double-clicking or placing it in the install folder does not activate it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A macOS VM user installs the Tricentis Automation Extension in Chrome on their macOS host. They then open Chrome inside their Windows VM and try to scan the SUT with XScan. XScan cannot detect the browser. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The extension is not compatible with the Chrome version inside the VM.
The extension was installed in the macOS host Chrome, not in the Chrome browser running inside the Windows VM.
XScan does not support Chrome — it only works with Firefox.
The Tosca license does not include web scanning capabilities.

practiceQuiz.hint: The extension must live in the same environment as Tosca.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Tricentis Automation Extension must be installed in the Chrome browser running inside the Windows VM — not the macOS host browser. Tosca communicates with the local Chrome instance in the VM, not the host OS browser.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After installation, a tester opens Tosca Commander and sees 'No valid license found'. What should they do?

options.text: Reinstall Tosca completely — the license was corrupted during installation.
Wait 24 hours — licenses activate automatically over the internet.
Navigate to Help → License → Import License File and select the .lic file received from Tricentis.
Copy the .lic file to the Tosca installation directory and restart.

practiceQuiz.hint: The license file must be explicitly imported via the Help menu.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A 'No valid license found' message means the license has not yet been imported. Navigate to Help → License → Import License File in Tosca Commander and select your .lic file to activate it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before starting the Tricentis Tosca AS1 course exercises, which THREE items must be confirmed as ready?

options.text: Tricentis Tosca On-Premises is installed and the license is active in Tosca Commander.
The Tricentis Automation Extension is installed and enabled in Google Chrome.
The demo SUT (https://demowebshop.tricentis.com) is accessible in Chrome.
A local test server for the demo web shop has been set up on the machine.

practiceQuiz.hint: The SUT is hosted online — no local server setup needed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The three prerequisites are: active Tosca installation with license (A), Tricentis Automation Extension in Chrome (B), and access to the hosted SUT at demowebshop.tricentis.com (C). No local server setup is required — the SUT is a publicly hosted web application. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the System Under Test (SUT) used throughout the AS1 course, and what setup does it require?

options.text: A local database you must install and configure.
Your own company's production website.
A desktop calculator app bundled with Tosca.
The Tricentis Demo Web Shop — hosted online, no local server setup required.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The course SUT is the Tricentis Demo Web Shop, hosted online — there is no local server to install. You automate against it directly in the browser.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where do you request a free training license for Tosca?

options.text: At the Tricentis Support Hub (support-hub.tricentis.com), with a Tricentis account.
From the Chrome Web Store.
Inside Tosca Commander under Help → Buy License.
Licenses are automatically included; no request needed.

practiceQuiz.hint: A Tricentis online portal issues training licenses.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Free training licenses are requested at the Tricentis Support Hub (support-hub.tricentis.com); you need a Tricentis account. You then import the received .lic file via Help → License → Import License File.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You plan to start the exercises next week. What is the best practice for timing your training license request?

options.text: Request it months ahead — licenses never expire.
Training licenses are typically valid 30–90 days, so request yours 1–2 days before you start.
Request a new license before every session.
No timing matters; licenses are permanent.

practiceQuiz.hint: They have a limited validity window.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Training licenses are typically valid for 30–90 days. Request yours 1–2 days before you plan to start so the validity window covers your study period.
